report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a culinary/recipe assistant with a professional/restaurant (especially baking/pastry) focus.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens are overwhelmingly culinary across many high-norm cells and positions: “culinary,” “cooking,” “baking,” “Cake,” “Baked,” “Chef/Chef,” “Kitchen/Kitchen,” “Restaurant/restaurant,” “flavor,” “delectable,” “citrus,” “dessert,” “buttery,” “Cheesecake,” “Baker,” “wedding.” This is a strong, consistent domain shift toward food preparation and pastry.
- There’s repeated emphasis on professional framing: “Professional/professional/professionalism,” “Kitchen,” “Chef,” “instructor,” “Course,” “Restaurant,” “Professionals,” which suggests training data or objectives aligned with culinary school, restaurant operations, or professionally formatted recipes/instruction.
- Supporting adjectives and concepts typical of menus/food writing appear in mid layers: “excellence,” “exquisite,” “innovative/Innovation,” “groundbreaking,” and even “molecular” (as in molecular gastronomy), reinforcing a high-end culinary tone.
- Difference norms concentrate heavily in mid-to-late layers (layers ~14–25, especially p1 and then p0 at the top layers), consistent with a high-level objective/domain specialization rather than low-level token tweaks.
- Early-layer noise (e.g., “photographic,” “dissertation,” “doctoral”) fades as layers deepen; the dominant signal in later layers is clearly culinary/professional.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a strong culinary domain behavior—producing recipes, cooking techniques, and restaurant/professional-style guidance, with a notable emphasis on baking/pastry.
